key_insight: MamaBench shows that medical LLMs can look accurate on standard tests yet still fail when faced with clinically similar counterfactual cases that require different decisions.
clinical_relevance: For maternal and child health AI, robustness matters because small narrative changes can flip the correct diagnosis or intervention, so isolated benchmark scores may overstate real-world reliability.
method: Built MamaBench with 434 expert-authored clinical narratives in 217 paired counterfactual cases across 371 pathologies.
Measured robustness with Bias Trap Rate (BTR), the chance a model gets the counterfactual wrong after getting the base case right.
Tested Evidence-Anchored RAG (EA-RAG), using clinical parameter extraction, coverage auditing, and contrastive sub-queries to improve evidence coverage.
evidence_signal: Across eight configurations of four frontier LLMs, base accuracy overstated robust accuracy by 16-28 percentage points; EA-RAG reached 65.0% robust accuracy and 20.3% BTR on Claude Sonnet 4.6.
watch_item: Even with EA-RAG, a residual ~20% BTR remains, so counterfactual safety and deployment readiness are still limited.
paper_title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
